heading.en: Why vinegar fizzes with baking soda

hook.en: Pour vinegar on baking soda and it fizzes. Phenol, though acidic, does nothing. The answer lies in how well each anion spreads its negative charge.
hook.kn: ಅಡಿಗೆ ಸೋಡಾದ ಮೇಲೆ ವಿನೆಗರ್ ಸುರಿದರೆ ನೊರೆ ಬರುತ್ತದೆ. ಫೀನಾಲ್ ಆಮ್ಲೀಯವಾದರೂ ಏನೂ ಆಗುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. ಉತ್ತರ ಪ್ರತಿ ಋಣ ಅಯಾನು ತನ್ನ ಆವೇಶವನ್ನು ಎಷ್ಟು ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿ ಹರಡುತ್ತದೆ ಎಂಬುದರಲ್ಲಿದೆ.

say.en: Why vinegar fizzes with baking soda. Pour vinegar on baking soda and it fizzes. Phenol, though acidic, does nothing. The answer lies in how well each anion spreads its negative charge. In this lesson: Explain the acidity of carboxylic acids and the effect of substituents.
Write reactions involving O-H, C-OH and -COOH cleavage.
Write HVZ and ring substitution reactions.

body.en: The carboxylate ion is stabilised by resonance between two equivalent oxygens, so carboxylic acids are stronger than phenols and release $CO_2$ from $NaHCO_3$. Electron-withdrawing groups increase *acidity*, more so the closer and the more of them; electron-donating groups decrease it. pKa: $CF_3COOH$ 0.23, $Cl_3CCOOH$ 0.65, $Cl_2CHCOOH$ 1.26, $ClCH_2COOH$ 2.86, HCOOH 3.75, $C_6H_5COOH$ 4.19, $CH_3COOH$ 4.76.
body.kn: ಕಾರ್ಬಾಕ್ಸಿಲೇಟ್ ಅಯಾನಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಋಣ ಆವೇಶವನ್ನು ಎರಡು ಆಕ್ಸಿಜನ್‌ಗಳು ಸಮವಾಗಿ ಹಂಚಿಕೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತವೆ; ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಕಾರ್ಬಾಕ್ಸಿಲಿಕ್ ಆಮ್ಲಗಳು ಫೀನಾಲ್‌ಗಿಂತ ಪ್ರಬಲ ಮತ್ತು NaHCO₃ ನೊಂದಿಗೆ ನೊರೆಯುತ್ತವೆ. ಹತ್ತಿರದ ಇಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್ ಆಕರ್ಷಕ ಗುಂಪುಗಳು ಆಮ್ಲೀಯತೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

narration.en: In the carboxylate ion the negative charge is shared equally by two oxygen atoms, so carboxylic acids are stronger than phenols and fizz with sodium bicarbonate. Electron withdrawing groups nearby make the acid even stronger.

title.en: Why acids are acidic, and what they do

say.en: A carboxylic acid gives a proton to water. The carboxylate ion spreads its negative charge equally over two oxygens.

text.en: Charge shared over two O atoms

say.en: The acid constant Ka measures strength. The smaller the pKa, the stronger the acid.
Electron-withdrawing groups stabilise the anion and lower the pKa. Chloroacetic acid is much stronger than acetic acid.
Reactions: with alcohols and acid they form esters; lithium aluminium hydride reduces them to primary alcohols.
Soda lime removes carbon dioxide from the sodium salt; the HVZ reaction puts a halogen on the alpha carbon.
Why acids are acidic, and what they do.

narration.en: Each acid is half ionised when pH = pKa. Electron-withdrawing groups (Cl, NO₂) stabilise the carboxylate ion and lower pKa; carboxylic acids are much stronger than phenol.
narration.kn: pH = pKa ಆದಾಗ ಪ್ರತಿ ಆಮ್ಲ ಅರ್ಧ ಅಯಾನೀಕೃತ. ಇಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್ ಸೆಳೆಯುವ ಗುಂಪುಗಳು (Cl, NO₂) ಕಾರ್ಬಾಕ್ಸಿಲೇಟ್ ಅಯಾನನ್ನು ಸ್ಥಿರಗೊಳಿಸಿ pKa ಇಳಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

body.en: O–H: salts with Na, NaOH and $NaHCO_3$. C–OH: esterification with alcohols (conc. $H_2SO_4$); acyl chlorides with $PCl_5$, $PCl_3$ or $SOCl_2$; amides with $NH_3$ on heating; anhydrides with $P_2O_5$. –COOH: $LiAlH_4$ reduces to 1° alcohols; sodium salts heated with soda lime lose $CO_2$ (decarboxylation, $RCOONa \rightarrow RH$); Kolbe electrolysis gives alkanes. Hydrocarbon part: Hell–Volhard–Zelinsky, $X_2$/red P gives α-halo acids. On a benzene ring –COOH is deactivating and meta-directing, and benzoic acid does not undergo Friedel–Crafts *reactions*.
body.kn: ಕಾರ್ಬಾಕ್ಸಿಲಿಕ್ ಆಮ್ಲಗಳು ಲವಣ, ಎಸ್ಟರ್, ಆಸಿಡ್ ಕ್ಲೋರೈಡ್ ಮತ್ತು ಅಮೈಡ್ ರೂಪಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. LiAlH₄ ಪ್ರಾಥಮಿಕ ಆಲ್ಕೋಹಾಲ್ ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ, ಸೋಡಾ ಸುಣ್ಣ CO₂ ತೆಗೆಯುತ್ತದೆ, HVZ ಕ್ರಿಯೆಯಲ್ಲಿ α-ಕಾರ್ಬನ್ ಹ್ಯಾಲೋಜನೀಕರಣಗೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತದೆ.

problem.en: pKa of chloroacetic acid is 2.86 and of acetic acid is 4.76. How many times stronger is chloroacetic acid?

narration.en: Let us solve this together. pKa of chloroacetic acid is 2.86 and of acetic acid is 4.76. How many times stronger is chloroacetic acid?

say.en: Let us solve this together. pKa of chloroacetic acid is 2.86 and of acetic acid is 4.76. How many times stronger is chloroacetic acid?
Ka ratio equals 10^4.76 minus 2.86 equals 10 to the power 1.90.
10 to the power 1.90 is approximately 79.
So the answer is About 79 times stronger.

problem.en: What mass of methane is formed when 8.2 g of sodium ethanoate is heated with excess soda lime? (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16, Na = 23)

narration.en: Let us solve this together. What mass of methane is formed when 8.2 g of sodium ethanoate is heated with excess soda lime? (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16, Na = 23)

say.en: Let us solve this together. What mass of methane is formed when 8.2 grams of sodium ethanoate is heated with excess soda lime? (C equals 12, H equals 1, O equals 16, Na equals 23).
CH 3COONa plus NaOH gives CH 4 plus Na 2CO 3 (1: 1).
CH 3COONa equals 24 plus 3 plus 32 plus 23 equals 82 grams per mole; 8.2 grams equals 0.1 moles.
CH 4 equals 16 grams per mole; mass equals 0.1 times 16 equals 1.6 grams.
So the answer is 1.6 grams of methane.

say.en: Pause and solve this exam pattern question. Which of the following is the strongest acid?
Halogens withdraw electrons by the -I effect and stabilise the carboxylate ion.
Fluorine is the most electronegative, so FCH 2COOH is the strongest acid here.

narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. ಕಾರ್ಬಾಕ್ಸಿಲೇಟ್ ಅನುರಣನದಿಂದ ಆಮ್ಲಗಳು ಫೀನಾಲ್‌ಗಿಂತ ಪ್ರಬಲ; NaHCO₃ ನೊಂದಿಗೆ ನೊರೆ. –COOH ಹತ್ತಿರದ ಇಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್ ಆಕರ್ಷಕ ಗುಂಪುಗಳು ಆಮ್ಲೀಯತೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. ಸೋಡಾ ಸುಣ್ಣ ಡಿಕಾರ್ಬಾಕ್ಸಿಲೀಕರಣ; LiAlH₄ ಪ್ರಾಥಮಿಕ ಆಲ್ಕೋಹಾಲ್ ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ. HVZ: X₂/ಕೆಂಪು P α-ಕಾರ್ಬನ್ ಅನ್ನು ಹ್ಯಾಲೋಜನೀಕರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: Let us recall the key ideas. Carboxylate resonance makes carboxylic acids stronger than phenols; they fizz with NaHCO 3.
say.kn: ಮುಖ್ಯ ಅಂಶಗಳನ್ನು ನೆನಪಿಸಿಕೊಳ್ಳೋಣ. ಕಾರ್ಬಾಕ್ಸಿಲೇಟ್ ಅನುರಣನದಿಂದ ಆಮ್ಲಗಳು ಫೀನಾಲ್‌ಗಿಂತ ಪ್ರಬಲ; NaHCO 3 ನೊಂದಿಗೆ ನೊರೆ.
